messages:
marta: Hey — running into failures when onboarding a customer to Dedicated. Async Python client to a private base_url behind an HTTP proxy keeps failing TLS verification even though we installed the cust CA.

marta: Error looks like `ssl.SSLCertVerificationError: certificate verify failed: unable to get local issuer certificate` when request hits our proxy.

marta: Quick snippet of how I'm creating the client:
```py
from redwood import RedwoodAsyncClient
client = RedwoodAsyncClient(api_key=KEY, base_url='https://dedicated.example.internal', verify='/etc/custom-ca/ca.pem')
```

alex: Do you set any proxy envs? HTTP(S)_PROXY or `trust_env` toggles with httpx can bite async flows.

marta: Yes `HTTPS_PROXY=https://proxy.company:3128` and `SSL_CERT_FILE=/etc/custom-ca/ca.pem` in the container. No other special flags.

sam: Which httpx version + which redwood-py? We had a bug where async client transport ignored `SSL_CERT_FILE` if proxies were in use (httpx 0.23 drift).

marta: redwood-py 0.14.2, httpx 0.23.3 in the image.

tim: Can you paste a short log (with debug) showing the handshake path? Also try reproducing with a small curl call using the same envs to rule out proxy doing MITM.

marta: Attach logs:
```
INFO  connection established to proxy.company:3128
DEBUG httpx.transports.http11  -> starting TLS handshake
ERROR  ssl  certificate verify failed: unable to get local issuer certificate
```

alex: If the proxy is doing TLS termination, you need the proxy's CA in the truststore, not the origin's. But if it's a CONNECT proxy (tunnel), then the origin cert is what matters. Which is it?

marta: It's a forward proxy that terminates TLS for outbound traffic (corp gateway). We added the corp CA to the container, but the async calls still fail. The sync `requests`-based sample works.

sam: Aha — that matches prior reports. httpx async + proxy + `SSL_CERT_FILE` sometimes doesn't pick up the file unless you pass the cert path directly to the AsyncClient transport, because httpx trust lookup vs env precedence is inconsistent.

marta: Any recommended quick patch? Customer needs onboarding this week.

tim: Two options: 1) set `trust_env=False` and pass `verify='/etc/custom-ca/ca.pem'` explicitly when constructing the client (forces httpx to use that file), or 2) create an AsyncClient with a custom SSLContext and pass it in. Example:
```py
import ssl
from httpx import AsyncClient
ctx = ssl.create_default_context(cafile='/etc/custom-ca/ca.pem')
client = AsyncClient(verify=ctx, proxies={'https':'https://proxy.company:3128'})
# then hand this session into redwood lib if we expose a session hook
```

marta: Tried option 1 (trust_env=False + verify path) — still failing. Option 2: creating explicit SSLContext worked in a quick repro.

devx-bot: FYI queued a follow-up ticket DEVEX-4217 to explore exposing an `httpx_client_factory` or `transport` param on RedwoodAsyncClient so users can inject custom AsyncClient/SSLContexts.

alex: We should also document this in the Dedicated onboarding guide (custom CA + corporate proxies). It's a common enterprise gotcha.

marta: Filed a short doc PR with repro + workaround. Will link to ticket.

sam: Long-term we probably want the SDK to accept a `ssl_context` or `transport` argument to avoid users needing to construct httpx internals. Raising an SDK feature request.

infra-bot: @marta deployed image `onboard-1723` to staging at 2025-11-09T14:03Z — includes httpx upgrade to 0.23.5 for testing.

marta: After upgrading httpx to 0.23.5, still hit the issue unless SSLContext is provided. So marking that as our recommended workaround for now.

tim: Follow-up checklist for DEVEX-4217: (1) add `ssl_context`/`transport` arg to Async client ctor, (2) document proxy+CA pitfalls in onboarding, (3) add unit/integration test that spins a MITM proxy and asserts verify flow.

marta: Customer is unblocked now. We'll keep the ticket open for the SDK change. Thanks all :raised_hands:
